doc.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Australian quartet with Mike Nock and a commercial fusion date
summary: A record made after a Jamey clinic in Australia with Mike Nock, plus a commercial fusion session for Japanese keyboardist Sato.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Here’s an interesting record – a couple of them. One is the quartet record in Australia with Mike Nock, Ron McClure, and Ed Soph.

It comes out of a Jamey clinic, and then we stayed and did a couple dates. Horst Liepolt had this label, the guy who ran Sweet Basil. He had this label, and that’s how this record came out. That’s a good record. That record, a lot of people know I Concentrate on You, my arrangement of I Concentrate on You. I solo on that, because I put – I reharmonized. I put a little Coltrane thing in it, blah blah blah. That is a very burning record. Mike Nock’s a bad boy, I tell you. That’s a bad boy.
Yeah. He’s back in Sydney now.

I’ve seen Mike. We did a duo record. We won the Grammy of the year a couple years ago. We did it when I went to Wangaratta. We had never – we hadn’t played since then. They put us together at a midnight show. They recorded it, radio. We put it out as a record. He did a record that is his pieces played by a classical piano player. It’s fantastic, written pieces, classical. Really happening. He didn’t play. It’s his. It’s about 20 of his pieces. It’s a masterpiece. He’s great. Mike’s way up there.
Next is Mashiko Sato, the Japanese keyboard player.
I don’t remember it really, except that’s one of those Japanese combinations.
This is a funny but interesting band: Randy Brecker, Barry Rogers, Dave Taylor, Tom Malone, you, Sato, Ryo Kawasaki, Francisco Santino on bass, and Harvey Mason on drums.
That’s a commercial fusion record. That’s an absolute fusion record.
